patterns.block_scope_state_reset: R63 #aw_sg63a1 bufferresetbeforereuse: a write/read/reset state machine re-initialized fresh PER *ast.BlockStmt (analyzeStraightLineBlock's written/read maps), combined with collectEvents refusing to descend into If/For/Range/Switch/TypeSwitch/Select, means state never carries from an outer block into a nested control-flow block. A write+read in the outer scope followed by a reuse-write inside a nested if/for is invisible - the inner block's isolated event list sees only a first-ever write. PROBE any linter/analyzer that (a) walks every BlockStmt via ast.Inspect calling a per-block analysis function, AND (b) has that per-block function refuse to descend into sibling control-flow bodies - the two together silently sever state that should span the whole function. PROBE any new linter that walks blocks independently for a per-block-only forward search.
patterns.idiom_reflag_no_allowlist: R67 #61024 blankassigncomma (71st linter, first audit): a bare-syntax rule (2+ consecutive blank identifiers on an assignment LHS) with no allow-list or comment-aware exception re-flags an already-established codebase idiom for explicitly discarding a guaranteed-safe or non-critical return value (14 prod sites found, one with an explicit gosec-satisfying comment one line above it: hash.Hash.Write never returns an error in practice, but check to satisfy gosec G104). Root cause class: the new linter targets exactly the syntactic shape that contributors already use as the MANUAL workaround for a different, broken or disabled tool (here, errcheck exclude-functions, disabled in .golangci.yml:37) - so the new rule fights the old rules own accepted workaround instead of the actual bug. PROBE any new linter whose target pattern (a) has zero type-awareness of a well-known safe-to-ignore return contract (hash.Hash.Write, Close() on some best-effort cleanup, etc), and (b) is not cross-checked against grep of the real codebase before deciding readiness - a rule with a very simple AST shape and no allow-list is the highest-risk case for this class.
patterns.paren_unwrap_gap: R69 #61519 nilctxpassed: isBuiltinNil bare expr.(*ast.Ident), no unwrap. R70 #61715: errstringmatch isErrDotError bare *ast.CallExpr assertion + sprintfbool bare *ast.BasicLit assertion, both no unwrap. R71 #61948: root cause traced ONE LAYER DOWN into shared astutil.StringLitValue (astutil.go:745) + astutil.IsStringLiteral (astutil.go:49), both bare expr.(*ast.BasicLit) with no UnwrapParenExpr - since these are reused helpers (not per-linter code), the gap silently affects 5 call sites at once: trimleftright, tolowerequalfold(literal side), errstringmatch, and transitively fmterrorfnoverbs+errorfwrapv via ResolveFormatString's StringLitValue base case. tolowerequalfold ALSO has its own separate call-side gap (caseConvFuncAndArg bare *ast.CallExpr, same as the errstringmatch/sprintfbool class) - bundled both into sg71a2. Reference fix idiom used correctly elsewhere: walkfuncerrshadow/mapdeletecheck/packagelevelmutableslicemap/typeassertionokdiscarded. R72: exhaustively re-grepped astutil.go for remaining bare *ast.BasicLit/*ast.Ident/*ast.CallExpr assertions - ALL remaining instances (AsStringsMethodCall, HasConstantStringArg, IsFmtErrorf, IsPkgSelector, IsRegexpCompileCall, TwoValueTypeAssertionOKIdent) are either paren-immune by Go grammar (bare package identifiers cannot be parenthesized in a qualified-ident position), pre-unwrapped by every real caller before the call, or backed by a paren-transparent go/types constant-value fallback. VEIN NOW EXHAUSTED for astutil.go shared helpers beyond the still-open sg71a2 fix itself; do not re-probe astutil.go for this class again unless new helper functions are added.
patterns.branch_state_merge: R72 #62115 httprespbodyclose (first-ever solo bug audit of this linter beyond its original FuncLit-scope fixes #43465/#43526): respVars is a single map keyed by types.Object, populated by ONE flat ast.Inspect over the whole function/FuncLit body with no control-flow branch scoping. A manual (non-deferred) Body.Close() in one if/else branch and a defer Body.Close() of the SAME variable in the sibling, mutually-exclusive branch both write into the SAME respVarState entry - hasManualClose becomes true from one branch, hasDeferClose becomes true from the other, and the combined hasManualClose&&!hasDeferClose guard evaluates false, silently masking a real manual-close violation that independently matches the linters own BadManualClose pattern. Root cause: the state model tracks one event history per RESOURCE VARIABLE across the whole function, not per REACHABLE PATH, so two mutually-exclusive branches get incorrectly OR-ed together as if they were sequential/cumulative facts about one linear execution. PROBE any other per-object resource-lifecycle linter with a single shared map/state entry per variable (manualmutexunlock, fileclosenotdeferred, contextcancelnotdeferred, wgdonenotdeferred, resourcetracker-framework linters) for the same if/else sibling-branch conflation - distinct from the already-checked nested_selector_key_collapse (which is about KEY COMPUTATION, not event merging across branches).
